meta.scope: Afghanistan Batch 5 — Climate/drought/water stress and provincial densification (Kabul, Herat, Balkh) under highly constrained conditions.

candidates.title: Drought and water-stress statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from climate monitoring and humanitarian sources
candidates.description: Statistics and monitoring on drought conditions, snowpack, soil moisture and water availability. Recurrent drought is a primary driver of food insecurity and rural livelihood stress; western and southern provinces are frequently the most affected.
candidates.notes: High-centrality environmental constraint node linking agriculture and humanitarian needs.

candidates.title: Kabul province economic and demographic framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from spatial and statistical sources
candidates.description: Framing of Kabul province as the dominant urban, administrative and services centre. Concentrates a large share of the national urban population and economic activity relative to other provinces.

candidates.title: Herat province economic and trade framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from spatial and trade sources
candidates.description: Framing of Herat as the principal western commercial and trade hub, with strong links to Iran and a large urban population. Frequently ranks among the more economically active provinces outside Kabul.

candidates.title: Balkh province economic and trade framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from spatial and trade sources
candidates.description: Framing of Balkh (including Mazar-i-Sharif) as the principal northern commercial and trade hub, with links to Uzbekistan and Central Asia. An important secondary urban and economic pole.

candidates.title: Afghanistan climate–provincial densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from climate and spatial sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding drought/water-stress statistics and the Kabul, Herat and Balkh provincial framings into a coherent environmental and spatial layer under highly constrained conditions.
